### Building a New PC – Step‑by‑Step Guide Below is a practical, beginner‑friendly walkthrough. Feel free to skip sections you already know, but keep the order for best results. | # | Step | What to Do | Tips | |---|------|------------|------| | 1 | **Plan & Budget** | • Decide what you’ll use it for (gaming, video editing, office, etc.)
• Set a budget (CPU, GPU, RAM, storage, case, PSU, peripherals). | Use online PC builders (PCPartPicker, BuildMyPC) to compare prices and check compatibility. | | 2 | **Gather Components** | • CPU (Intel/AMD)
• Motherboard (socket, chipset, form‑factor)
• RAM (DDR4/DDR5, speed, capacity)
• GPU (if not integrated)
• Storage (SSD/HDD, NVMe or SATA)
• Power Supply Unit (PSU, wattage, 80+ rating)
• Case (ATX, mATX, mini‑ITX, size, airflow)
• Cooling (stock cooler, aftermarket air cooler, AIO liquid cooler)
• Operating System (Windows, Linux, etc.) | Check compatibility lists (e.g., CPU‑to‑Motherboard socket, PSU connectors). | | 3 | **Prepare Workspace** | • Clean, flat, static‑free surface.
• Anti‑static wrist strap or anti‑static mat.
• Screwdrivers (Phillips #0, #1). | Avoid carpeted floors; static can damage components. | | 4 | **Install the CPU** | • Open the motherboard’s CPU socket latch.
• Align the CPU (gold triangle) with the socket.
• Gently place it, then lock the latch. | Don’t force; the socket will guide. | | 5 | **Apply Thermal Paste & Install Cooler** | • If using an aftermarket cooler, apply a pea‑size amount of thermal paste on the CPU.
• Mount the cooler according to its instructions. | Many coolers come with pre‑applied paste; skip if so. | | 6 | **Insert RAM** | • Open the RAM slots’ clips.
• Align the notch on the RAM stick with the slot.
• Push firmly until the clips click. | Install in pairs for dual‑channel mode. | | 7 | **Mount the Motherboard in the Case** | • Align standoffs in the case with motherboard holes.
• Screw the motherboard onto the standoffs. | Use the correct screw length; avoid overtightening. | | 8 | **Install Storage** | • Mount SSD/HDD in drive bays or M.2 slot.
• Secure with screws or retention clips. | For NVMe, insert into the M.2 slot at a slight angle, then lock. | | 9 | **Install the Power Supply** | • Place PSU in its compartment (usually bottom rear).
• Secure with screws.
• Route cables neatly. | Keep the PSU fan facing out of the case for airflow. | | 10 | **Connect Power Cables** | • 24‑pin ATX to motherboard.
• 8‑pin (or 4‑pin) CPU power.
• GPU power (6‑pin, 8‑pin, or both).
• SATA power to drives. | Label cables or use color‑coded connectors for easier troubleshooting. | | 11 | **Connect Data Cables** | • SATA data to motherboard for HDD/SSD.
• M.2 data is already seated.
• Front panel connectors (USB, audio, power button, reset). | Refer to motherboard manual for exact pin layout. | | 12 | **Install GPU** | • Remove the appropriate expansion slot cover on the case.
• Insert GPU into the top PCI‑e x16 slot.
• Secure with screws. | Ensure the GPU is fully seated; the slot should click. | | 13 | **Cable Management** | • Tidy up cables using Velcro ties or zip ties.
• Route cables through the case’s cable‑management holes. | Good airflow and easier future upgrades. | | 14 | **Final Checks** | • Double‑check all connections.
• Ensure no loose screws or cables touching components.
• Verify that the PSU fan is spinning. | Turn off power before opening the case again. | | 15 | **Power On & BIOS Setup** | • Connect monitor, keyboard, mouse.
• Power on the system.
• Enter BIOS (usually DEL or F2).
• Check that CPU, RAM, storage are recognized. | Update BIOS if needed (download from motherboard manufacturer). | | 16 | **Install Operating System** | • Create a bootable USB with Windows or Linux.
• Boot from USB and follow installation prompts.
• Install drivers (GPU, chipset, Wi‑Fi). | Keep the system connected to the internet for updates. | | 17 | **Test & Benchmark** | • Run stress tests (Prime95, 3DMark, Cinebench).
• Monitor temperatures (HWMonitor, MSI Afterburner). | Ensure temperatures stay within safe limits. | | 18 | **Enjoy & Maintain** | • Keep drivers updated.
• Clean dust from fans every 3–6 months.
• Monitor performance and tweak settings. | Regular maintenance prolongs lifespan. | --- #### Quick Checklist - [ ] CPU + cooler installed - [ ] RAM seated - [ ] Motherboard mounted - [ ] PSU installed - [ ] Storage mounted - [ ] GPU installed - [ ] All power/data cables connected - [ ] Front panel connectors attached - [ ] Cable management tidy - [ ] BIOS recognizes all components - [ ] OS installed and drivers updated #### Common Pitfalls | Issue | Fix | |-------|-----| | **CPU not seated** | Re‑open socket, align correctly, lock latch. | | **RAM not recognized** | Install in correct slots (dual‑channel), ensure proper orientation. | | **GPU not detected** | Check PCI‑e slot, secure power connectors, update BIOS. | | **No boot** | Verify power supply is switched on, check all cables, ensure monitor input is correct. | | **High temperatures** | Improve airflow, reapply thermal paste, clean dust. | --- ### Resources - **PCPartPicker** – component compatibility checker and price comparison. - **YouTube Channels** – Linus Tech Tips, JayzTwoCents, Paul's Hardware for visual guides. - **Manufacturer Manuals** – always read the motherboard, PSU, and case manuals for specifics. Happy building! If you hit a snag, let me know which step and I’ll help troubleshoot.
message.reasoning: User asks "How to build a new PC?" They want instructions. We can provide a step-by-step guide. No function call needed.
